selected_script.angle: dull scuffed hardwood haze from ordinary damp wiping that makes fine scratches look worse
selected_script.hook: extreme close-up of a homeowner scrubbing a cloudy scuffed hardwood patch with a damp paper towel, but the haze spreads instead of improving

timeline.0-3s: Extreme close-up on a warm hardwood floor with dull cloudy haze, light scuffs, and fine surface scratches near a kitchen walkway. A hand tries the familiar ordinary method: scrubbing with a damp paper towel. The towel drags across the same spot, but the floor still looks flat and streaky.
timeline.3-6s: The same damp paper towel keeps rubbing harder in small circles. The haze spreads into visible streaks, tiny water smears catch the light, and the hand pauses with mild frustration because the scratches and dull patch look even more obvious.
timeline.6-10s: The DAXAXA Wood Floor Restorer & Polish 16oz bottle enters naturally beside the same stain area. A small amount is applied to a clean flat mop pad and spread evenly with the wood grain on the exact same section. After a realistic quick jump cut to the dried finish, the camera tilts low to show a credible split between untreated dull wood and the treated glossy area with softened-looking fine scratches, cleaner reflection, and no greasy footprints. Light spoken CTA: 'Try DAXAXA for worn-looking wood floors.'

scenes.promptText:
Create one complete approximately 10-second vertical TikTok-style UGC cleaning-product ad in 9:16, realistic handheld phone-shot style, natural indoor kitchen or hallway lighting, close and tactile, no polished commercial look. Use the provided product reference images as the exact product identity: DAXAXA Wood Floor Restorer & Polish 16oz must remain a tall glossy red plastic bottle with rounded shoulders, narrow neck, ribbed blue screw cap, blue front label with yellow upper panel and cyan diagonal accent, small red brand badge near upper left, Hardwood Polish identity, realistic label proportions, material, color, shape, size ratio, cap structure, texture, and visible bottle details. Do not change the product color, label, shape, material, proportions, logo position, or visible structure. Do not invent accessories, sprayers, buttons, lights, packaging, tools attached to the bottle, or exaggerated functions. Use the detail and side reference image to preserve product material, side structure, edge shape, texture, and visible details. Use the function reference image only to understand real product usage; do not invent new functions.

Timeline inside this single video only:
0-3s: Start with an extreme close-up of a credible cleaning pain on a warm hardwood floor: a dull cloudy worn patch with fine scuffs and light surface scratches near a busy walkway. Do not start with a perfect product shot. A real hand uses a familiar ordinary method, a damp white paper towel, rubbing the scuffed dull patch back and forth. The towel leaves faint moisture streaks and the haze does not improve. Keep the shot tight enough to see wood grain, small scratches, and the failed wipe marks.
3-6s: Continue the same failed method on the exact same floor area. The hand rubs harder in small circles, the paper towel bunches slightly, the water smears catch the light, and the dull patch looks more streaky and frustrating. Show effort and failure realistically: no dramatic damage, no fake chemical smoke, no magical effects, just a normal damp wipe making the cloudy residue and fine scratches more visible.
6-10s: The DAXAXA Wood Floor Restorer & Polish bottle enters naturally from the side and is set beside the same worn patch, label facing camera and readable enough to identify the product without adding any on-screen text. A small amount is applied to a clean flat mop pad or soft cloth, then spread thinly and evenly in one direction with the wood grain over the exact same area. Include a credible quick jump cut implying the finish has dried, then show proof: a low handheld tilt across a clear before-after boundary where the untreated side remains dull and streaky while the treated side has a realistic high-gloss refreshed reflection and softened-looking fine surface scratches. End with the bottle standing on the restored area and a light natural spoken CTA only: 'Try DAXAXA for worn-looking wood floors.'

Keep the video realistic and physically plausible for a floor polish/restorer: thin even application, no instant magical disappearance, no exaggerated mirror effect, no harsh chemical reaction. Forbid UI, subtitles, captions, stickers, text overlays, watermarks, floating labels, arrows, icons, comparison graphics, invented claims, invented accessories, product drift, scene splitting, or extra products. The product must remain visible and central in the final seconds, with the same stain/patch clearly used for the failed method and the product result.
